# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible rival that fits every canonical demonstration is:

> Ignore the color-1 template and recolor **every** color-3 cell with the most frequent non-`{0,1,3}` marker color; clear everything else.

It fits all four usable canonical pairs because every canonical color-3 component happens to be a true template match. `checks/question-generator-shortcuts/counterexample.json` records `canonical_fit: [true, true, true, true]`.

An exact generated counterexample is seed `0`, sample index `0`, difficulty `easy`, with overrides `grid_h=10`, `grid_w=12`, `template_shape=l3`, `n_matches=1`, `n_distractors=1`, `majority_color=2`, `majority_count=2`, and `n_marker_colors=2`:

```text
000000000000
000000000000
000000000000
000000000000
333030000100
000033000110
000000000000
000000000000
000000000000
900000002020
```

The color-1 template is the L-tromino at rows 4–5, columns 9–10. The matching green L is at rows 4–5, columns 4–5. The horizontal green tromino at row 4, columns 0–2 is an equal-area nonmatch. Marker color 2 occurs twice, while 9 occurs once.

The intended output paints only the matching L with color 2. The shortcut additionally paints cells `(4,0)`, `(4,1)`, and `(4,2)`. I checked the intended output with the selected canonical Racket rule using:

```text
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 6145142974ff --input ../checks/question-generator-shortcuts/input.json --out ../checks/question-generator-shortcuts/racket.json
```

The command ran from the packet root wrapper, whose effective payload directory was `repo`. The Racket report records rule hash `d5061c3b9df5`, generator SHA-256 `74f509e69fc179963d3295401f9f81b4d9db6c60760a0cb0837724350751a012`, a valid output, and three differing cells versus the rival.

Yes—the proposed generator emits such cases by construction. Every ordinary draw has at least one nonmatching green component, and at least one has the same cell count as the template. The three-slot lesson schedule therefore refutes both recolor-all-green and cell-count-only rules in every lesson; the 300-lesson census confirms this for all sampled lessons.
